groups.title: Rate Controller
groups.hint: The innermost loop: it turns a rate setpoint into motor torque, and it is the loop responsible for how the aircraft feels. Tune it first, because every outer loop is built on top of it, and this is the one the autotune tunes.

fields.label: Roll rate P
fields.hint: Proportional gain on the rate error. Raise until the axis feels crisp, back off before it buzzes.

fields.label: Roll rate I
fields.hint: Integral gain. Removes steady-state error (wind, an off-centre payload) and is what a slow drift back to level comes from.

fields.label: Roll rate D
fields.hint: Derivative gain. Damps overshoot; too much of it amplifies motor and frame noise into heat.

fields.label: Roll rate feed-forward
fields.hint: Feed-forward from the rate setpoint. Improves tracking without touching the loop's stability.

fields.label: Roll rate gain
fields.hint: Overall gain multiplier for this axis. Scales P, I and D together, so it is the one knob to turn after a payload change.

fields.label: Roll integrator limit
fields.hint: Ceiling on the integrator, in normalised torque. Stops a long-held error from winding up into a lurch when the vehicle is released.

fields.label: Yaw rate feed-forward

groups.title: Attitude Controller
groups.hint: Turns an angle error into the rate setpoint the loop above feeds to the rate controller. Only worth touching once the rate loop tracks cleanly.

fields.label: Roll P
fields.hint: Turns a roll angle error into a roll rate setpoint. Higher is sharper; too high and the rate loop is asked for more than the airframe can give.

fields.label: Pitch P
fields.hint: Pitch angle error to pitch rate setpoint.

fields.label: Yaw P
fields.hint: Heading error to yaw rate setpoint.

fields.label: Yaw weight
fields.hint: How much yaw authority may be taken from roll and pitch when the mixer saturates. Lower keeps the vehicle upright at the cost of heading.

fields.label: Maximum roll rate
fields.hint: Ceiling on the rate setpoint the attitude loop may request.

tune.text: PX4 sets the attitude gains in the same run as the rate controller, so this starts that run.

groups.title: Velocity Controller
groups.hint: Holds a commanded speed. This is the loop behind a hover that drifts in wind or an altitude that sags as the battery does. PX4 has no autotune for it. These gains are set by hand.

fields.label: Horizontal velocity P
fields.hint: Horizontal velocity error to acceleration setpoint.

fields.label: Horizontal velocity I
fields.hint: Trims out a steady wind. Too high and the vehicle circles its hold point.

fields.label: Horizontal velocity D
fields.hint: Damps the velocity loop. Sensitive to position noise, so raise it slowly.

fields.label: Vertical velocity P
fields.hint: Vertical velocity error to acceleration setpoint.

fields.label: Vertical velocity I
fields.hint: Carries the hover thrust. This is the gain that holds altitude when the battery sags.

fields.label: Maximum tilt in flight
fields.hint: Caps the lean angle the velocity loop may ask for, and with it the horizontal acceleration the vehicle can produce.

fields.label: Hover throttle
fields.hint: The throttle that holds a hover. A wrong value makes every altitude change start with a lurch.

tune.text: PX4 has no autotune for this loop. Set the gains by hand, on the ground.

groups.title: Position Controller
groups.hint: The outermost loop: position error to velocity setpoint, plus the acceleration and jerk limits that decide how abrupt the vehicle is.

fields.label: Horizontal position P
fields.hint: Horizontal position error to velocity setpoint. Raise for a tighter hold, lower if the vehicle hunts around its hold point.

fields.label: Vertical position P
fields.hint: Altitude error to climb-rate setpoint.

fields.label: Jerk limit (missions)
fields.hint: How abruptly acceleration may change. Lower is smoother and gentler on a camera; higher tracks a mission leg more tightly.

tune.text: PX4 has no autotune for this loop. Set the gains by hand, on the ground.

groups.title: Autotune
groups.hint: PX4 tunes the rate and attitude controllers together, in flight, by injecting steps and measuring what came back.
groups.label: Multicopter autotune

axes.label: Axes to tune
axes.reason: PX4 tunes roll, pitch and yaw one after the other in a single run. Its multicopter autotune has no axis selection, so one axis cannot be tuned on its own. Any gain can still be set by hand in the Rate Controller below.

groups.running_text: The autopilot is exciting each axis in turn and measuring the response. Keep your hands off the sticks and hold the hover. Stop the tune at any time if the vehicle misbehaves.
groups.done_text: The tune finished. The gains were not applied because the apply setting is Never, so nothing on the vehicle has changed.
steps: Fly somewhere open, with room to drift, and keep a hand on the sticks.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Position or Altitude mode, 3-10 m up.
Start the tune and let go of the sticks. The autopilot injects its own steps and needs a clean response to measure.
Expect roughly a minute of visible twitching, one axis at a time.
Land and disarm to apply the gains, then test them gently before flying the aircraft normally.

fields.label: Autotune module
fields.hint: The module has to be running before it can be commanded. Switching this on takes effect after the autopilot reboots.

fields.label: Apply the tuned gains
fields.hint: When the result reaches the controller. Applying in flight is supported but leaves you flying gains nobody has checked.

fields.label: Excitation amplitude
fields.hint: How hard the autotune shakes the vehicle. Raise it on a large or heavy airframe whose response is otherwise lost in the noise; lower it if the aircraft feels alarming during the tune.

fields.label: Target rise time
fields.hint: The closed-loop response the tune aims for. Smaller means sharper and hotter motors.

Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.

steps: Fly somewhere open, in calm air, with plenty of altitude.
Trim the aircraft in FBWA so it flies straight and level hands-off.

steps: Fly somewhere open and calm. The tune needs room to drift and is thrown off by wind.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Loiter or AltHold, 5-10 m up.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.

steps: Fly somewhere open and calm. The tune needs room to drift and is thrown off by wind.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Loiter or AltHold, 5-10 m up.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.

groups.running_text: ArduPilot is tuning in AUTOTUNE mode, one axis at a time, and reports progress in the console rather than as a percentage. Keep the sticks centred: a nudge only pauses the tune. When the console says it is complete, land with the mode still AUTOTUNE and disarm to keep the gains.

steps: Fly somewhere open and calm. The tune needs room to drift and is thrown off by wind.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Loiter or AltHold, 5-10 m up.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.

field.label: Axes to tune
field.hint: Choose on the ground: parameters cannot be written while armed. One axis per flight takes longer, but a tune that misbehaves is easier to abort.

groups.running_text: ArduPilot is tuning in AUTOTUNE mode, one axis at a time, and reports progress in the console rather than as a percentage. Keep the sticks centred: a nudge only pauses the tune. When the console says it is complete, land with the mode still AUTOTUNE and disarm to keep the gains.
groups.done_text: ArduPilot is tuning in AUTOTUNE mode, one axis at a time, and reports progress in the console rather than as a percentage. Keep the sticks centred: a nudge only pauses the tune. When the console says it is complete, land with the mode still AUTOTUNE and disarm to keep the gains.
steps: Fly somewhere open and calm. The tune needs room to drift and is thrown off by wind.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Loiter or AltHold, 5-10 m up.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.

fields.label: Aggressiveness

fields.label: Minimum D
fields.hint: Floor on the D term, so the tune cannot leave an axis undamped.

groups.title: Rate Controller
groups.hint: The innermost loop: it turns a rate setpoint into control output, and it is the loop responsible for how the aircraft feels. Tune it first, because every outer loop is built on top of it, and this is the one the autotune tunes.

fields.label: Roll rate P
fields.hint: The main gain: how hard the controller reacts to a rate error. Raise it until the aircraft feels crisp, back off at the first sign of a twitch.

fields.label: Roll rate I
fields.hint: Removes steady error: a persistent lean from an off-centre payload or a bent arm. On ArduPilot this normally tracks P.

fields.label: Roll rate D
fields.hint: Damps the response. Too much amplifies motor and frame noise into heat.

fields.label: Roll integrator limit
fields.hint: Ceiling on the integrator's share of the output, as a fraction of full authority.

fields.label: Roll feed-forward
fields.hint: Passes the rate setpoint straight through, ahead of the error loop.

fields.label: Roll target filter
fields.hint: Low-pass on the setpoint entering the loop.

fields.label: Roll error filter
fields.hint: Low-pass on the rate error. Lowering it calms a noisy airframe at the cost of response.

fields.label: Roll derivative filter

groups.title: Autotune
groups.hint: ArduPilot's autotune is a flight mode, not a command: starting it switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE and the autopilot takes over from there. It narrates its progress over the console.
groups.label: AUTOTUNE mode
groups.running_text: ArduPilot is tuning in AUTOTUNE mode, one axis at a time, and reports progress in the console rather than as a percentage. Keep the sticks centred: a nudge only pauses the tune. When the console says it is complete, land with the mode still AUTOTUNE and disarm to keep the gains.
groups.done_text: ArduPilot is tuning in AUTOTUNE mode, one axis at a time, and reports progress in the console rather than as a percentage. Keep the sticks centred: a nudge only pauses the tune. When the console says it is complete, land with the mode still AUTOTUNE and disarm to keep the gains.
steps: Fly somewhere open and calm. The tune needs room to drift and is thrown off by wind.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Loiter or AltHold, 5-10 m up.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.
